items.title: LFM2.5-24B-A2B: Built for fast on-device agents

editorial.brief: Netflix's trailer for Narnia: The Magician's Nephew drew 24,495,690 YouTube views and also turned up on Wikipedia, which makes it the strongest two-feed story of the day. A model called LFM2.5-24B-A2B did the same across Hacker News and Hugging Face. Katie Zacharia led Wikipedia by 2.2x with no visible cause.
editorial.cover_sub: Katie Zacharia drew 906,890 reads, 2.2 times the runner-up, on a day when the other feeds were busy with a Narnia trailer and a prediction market on interest rates.
editorial.wiki_deck: Katie Zacharia took 906,890 Wikipedia views, more than double RJ Mitte in second place. Nothing else in the snapshot says why.
editorial.letter_headline: A Narnia trailer and a lot of unexplained traffic
editorial.discourse_deck: Hacker News is reading about cancer and dentistry, Lemmy about work, bathrooms and politics, Bluesky about a shorter Brazilian workweek and pumpkin bread, and Mastodon about goats, abandoned buildings and exhaustion with programmers.
editorial.foreign_deck: The wire brought over $100 million for US STEM and a McDonald's AI pricing suit; India searched ipo gmp, Germany 15. oktober, the US Florence Pugh.
editorial.markets_deck: Rates lead: 75% that the Fed holds, on $3M. Indiana's data center moratorium is 14% on $2M, two sports matches read 0% yes, Democrats holding the House is 91%.
editorial.watch_deck: Counter-Strike 2 peaked at 1,280,126 players, ahead of Dota 2 at 859,106 and PUBG at 803,114. On Twitch, caseoh_ holds 74,458 viewers, with TheBurntPeanut at 40,356 and Dantes at 25,481.
editorial.yt_note: Two trailers hold the list, Narnia at 24,495,690 views and Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 at 1,278,868. Narnia's total is more than 19 times that of Edgerunners.
editorial.closing_note: By tomorrow, Katie Zacharia's 906,890 reads will have dispersed to wherever such things go, and the goats, the pumpkin bread and Inktober day 14 will have scrolled off. The M5.9 near Fiji will be a footnote. Mathematics can wait.
wiki_paras: Katie Zacharia was the most-read article on Wikipedia in this snapshot, with 906,890 views. RJ Mitte followed with 409,408, and Mathematics took third with 236,760. The lead over second place was 2.2 times, which is a comfortable margin by any reading of the table.

The data offers no explanation. No other feed mentions the name. Google Trends has Florence Pugh, Natalie Portman and Witney Carson in the United States, but the data does not connect them to the article, and the news wire is occupied with STEM funding, pricing and graduates. Whoever drove the traffic left no trail in this snapshot.
